hero.audience: Independent policy analysis, action research and management consulting for governments, development partners, multilateral development banks, universities, think tanks and private-sector institutions.

scenes.title: Every hard public problem is several problems at once.
body: A fiscal squeeze shows up in schools. A heatwave shows up in the power grid. A weak institution turns a good budget into a stalled project.
The first job is to see how these pressures connect. Select a system to see what it is tied to.

scenes.title: Start with what can be checked.
body: We build the evidence base from five kinds of material and keep each one traceable to its source.
Layering them lets us test one against another, so a finding does not rest on a single number or a single interview.

scenes.title: Patterns become findings when they survive scrutiny.
body: Two questions come up in almost every engagement: did it work, and is it worth it? These diagrams show how we frame each one.

scenes.title: Findings become choices.
body: Evidence rarely points to a single answer. We set out the options, what each costs and risks, who has to act, and what implementation will take, so the decision is made with open eyes.

scenes.title: A decision only matters once it reaches a service.
body: Policy moves through ministries, agencies and municipalities into budgets, rules and front-line services. We help design the delivery arrangements, skills and monitoring that let a change hold.

scenes.title: Public value is something you can check later.
body: We agree how success will be recognised before the work starts, so results can be tracked, learned from and reported honestly.

systems.name: Economy
systems.note: Growth, jobs and public revenue set what governments can afford to do about everything else.

systems.name: Climate
systems.note: Heat, floods and drought hit harvests, grids and city budgets, and the transition reshapes the economy.

systems.name: Education
systems.note: Skills decide who can take the jobs growth creates, and schools are only as good as the budget and management behind them.

systems.name: Cities
systems.note: Growing cities need energy, water and transport, and the revenue to provide them.

systems.name: Energy
systems.note: Cost, reliability and emissions shape household welfare, business costs and climate targets at once.

systems.name: Institutions
systems.note: Laws, budgets and agencies decide whether any policy in this list reaches the people it is meant for.

evidence.name: Field research
evidence.text: Interviews, site visits and focus groups that show how a policy works on the ground.

evidence.name: Survey data
evidence.text: Household, firm and facility surveys, designed and sampled so the results can be generalised.

evidence.name: Administrative data
evidence.text: Budgets, registries and service records the state already holds.

evidence.name: Maps and spatial data
evidence.text: Where people, services and risks are, and how they relate to each other.

evidence.name: Evaluation methods
evidence.text: Designs that separate what a programme caused from what would have happened anyway.

charts.impactCaption: We compare change in the supported group with change in a similar group that was not supported. The gap beyond the dashed line is the estimated effect of the programme.
charts.costCaption: Costs come early and benefits build over time. The point where cumulative net benefit turns positive shows when the investment pays back. A full analysis also discounts future values and tests how the result changes under different assumptions.
charts.note: Illustrative example of the method, not project data.

policyExample: Worked example, hypothetical: a ministry must widen access to secondary school on a fixed budget.

policySteps.title: Findings
policySteps.text: Where children are missing out, and the reasons behind it.

policySteps.title: Options
policySteps.text: Three routes compared on the same terms.
choices: Build new schools where demand is growing

policySteps.title: Trade-offs
policySteps.text: Each option tested for what it costs, who benefits, how fast it works and how likely it is to succeed.

policySteps.title: Implementation choices
policySteps.text: Who delivers, how it is financed, which rules must change and how results will be tracked.

policySteps.title: Institutional decision
policySteps.text: A recommended option, the conditions attached to it and the indicators to watch after launch.

practiceStages.title: Institutions
practiceStages.text: Mandates, structures and procedures are set so the right body owns the change.

practiceStages.title: Programmes
practiceStages.text: Budgets, eligibility rules and delivery plans turn a policy into something a team can run.

practiceStages.title: Services
practiceStages.text: Schools, clinics, utilities and municipal offices receive the skills, tools and guidance to deliver.

practiceStages.title: Communities
practiceStages.text: Households and firms are reached, and their experience is fed back to decision-makers.

impactOutcomes.title: Stronger institutions
impactOutcomes.change: Clear mandates, budgets that are spent as planned, and decisions that can be traced to evidence.
impactOutcomes.shown: Budget execution, procurement and planning records, audit findings.

impactOutcomes.title: Better services
impactOutcomes.change: Services that reach more of the people entitled to them and work when they arrive.
impactOutcomes.shown: Coverage and quality measures from administrative data and user surveys.

impactOutcomes.title: More resilient systems
impactOutcomes.change: Public finances, infrastructure and programmes that absorb shocks instead of breaking under them.
impactOutcomes.shown: Stress tests, risk registers and performance through disruptions.

impactOutcomes.title: Improved lives
impactOutcomes.change: Households with better health, learning, income and security than they would otherwise have had.
impactOutcomes.shown: Evaluation designs that compare outcomes against a credible counterfactual.

film.heading: From the factory floor to the data room.
film.lead: Thirty seconds on how we work: start with the system, test what can be checked, and stay until policy works on the ground.
film.label: IP3 brand film: a garment factory sewing machine, climate and energy data on a touchscreen, IP3's circular economy projects title, and the IP3 logo with the line From polycrisis to polysolution.

terminal.heading: Policy Intelligence Terminal
terminal.lead: A governed execution platform for policy intelligence work. It watches tiered sources, merges what matters into one policy question, and turns it into briefs that show their evidence before anything is published.

beats.title: Every signal carries its evidence
beats.text: Live monitoring refreshes every five minutes. Each story arrives with its sources and their tier, the time it was fetched, and the ranking that put it on the board. Decision lenses re-read the same evidence for an executive, a macroeconomist, a development partner, a market analyst, a political economist or an academic.
beats.caption: Signals, sources and decision lenses

beats.title: Many discussions, one policy question
beats.text: The Merged Policy Discussion Studio connects the day's discussions into a single piece of directed research. The analyst sets the perspective, the question and the audience, chooses the discussions to merge, and keeps every source link visible.
beats.caption: Merged Policy Discussion Studio

beats.title: Modules built for IP3's missions
beats.text: MERLA, climate and ESG, and GovTech are native modules, not add-ons: outcome and milestone tracking with adaptive learning memos, adaptation finance and transition-risk maps, and digital public service maturity with reform roadmaps.
beats.caption: MERLA, Climate/ESG and GovTech modules

beats.title: Briefs that show their working
beats.text: The Brief Factory turns a story, the daily top ten or a fortnightly period into a brief. The original model draft, the refined policy brief, the evidence, each claim and its verification sit side by side before export.
beats.caption: Brief Factory: evidence, claims, verification, export
